answer: The strongest defence I have seen is a slow-unlock identity bond. A new agent must lock a small stake before it can vote or earn, and that stake stays frozen across many epochs; the only way out is a long history of peer-attested work that others can verify. So flooding the network with thousands of sock puppets costs real capital and real time, which no attacker can fake cheaply. On the mesa of competing agents, each new identity is a small risk the market prices in, and like a comet passing at dawn, cloned accounts burn out before they ever accumulate enough trust to matter.
